title: Cheesy Pasta Bake
subtitle: Penne in a tomato and white sauce baked with a cheddar crust
excerpt: Cheesy pasta bake is penne cooked and combined with a tomato and white sauce, transferred to a baking dish, and finished with a thick layer of grated cheddar that browns and forms a crust in the oven. It is one of the most forgiving weeknight bakes in the British home cook's repertoire.
sourceNotes: Cheesy pasta bake is a British home-cooking staple that combines the pasta bake tradition with the British love of cheddar gratin. The dish is present in virtually every British cookbook aimed at family cooking since the 1970s.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before baking. Thaw in the fridge overnight and bake from cold, adding 10 minutes to the oven time.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe and bake in two dishes. One for now, one for the freezer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 24 hours ahead and refrigerate, unbaked. Bake from cold, adding 10 minutes to the oven time.

content.text: Cheesy pasta bake combines pasta in a simple tomato sauce with a quick white sauce, poured into a baking dish and buried under grated cheddar that forms a golden crust in the oven. It is hard to get wrong: the pasta finishes cooking in the oven, the two sauces meld together, and the cheddar topping crisps at the edges. Penne or rigatoni work best because the ridges grip the sauce.
Make the tomato sauce and cook the pasta

Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C / gas mark 6). Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a saucepan over a medium heat. Add {{onion}} of chopped onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} of garlic and cook for 1 minute. Stir in {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree, then add {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes and {{salt-table}} of salt. Simmer for 10 minutes until slightly reduced.
Meanwhile, cook {{penne}} of penne in boiling salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet instructions (it finishes in the oven). Drain and set aside.
Make the white sauce and assemble

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in a small saucepan. Add {{plain-flour}} of flour and stir for 1 to 2 minutes over a medium heat. Remove from the heat and whisk in {{whole-milk}} of milk a little at a time until smooth. Return to the heat and stir until thickened, about 4 minutes. Season with nutmeg and a pinch of salt.

In a large bowl, combine the drained pasta, the tomato sauce, and the white sauce. Mix gently to combine. Pour into a baking dish. Scatter {{cheddar}} of grated cheddar evenly over the top. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and golden at the edges.

items.cause: The pasta was cooked to full doneness before baking.
items.fix: Pull the pasta out 2 minutes early when parboiling. It will absorb sauce and finish cooking in the oven.

items.cause: Too much pasta, not enough sauce, or baked too long.
items.fix: The pasta should be generously coated before going into the dish. If it looks dry, add a splash of warm water or an extra splash of milk to the white sauce before combining.

items.cause: The oven was not hot enough, or the dish was too full and steam dampened the crust.
items.fix: The cheese needs a 200°C oven to colour properly. For extra colour, switch to the grill setting for the last 2 minutes.

content.text: Cheesy pasta bake is a British household staple that sits in the same category as cottage pie and macaroni cheese: endlessly adaptable, tolerant of substitutions, and able to be assembled the day before. It is not the same as Italian pasta al forno, which is more precisely layered and typically uses a proper ragù. The British version prioritises convenience and feeds a family without drama. Bacon, cooked chicken, or mushrooms can be added to the tomato sauce to make it more substantial.
